events.title: Crosby v. Starr, Warden, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and dismissed the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Crosby v. Starr, Warden, et al. The Court also directed the Clerk not to accept further petitions from the petitioner in noncriminal matters without the required docketing fee due to repeated abuse of the Court's process.
events.why_relevant: This order addresses the misuse of the Court's process and imposes restrictions on future filings by the petitioner.

events.title: Flower Foods, Inc., et al. v. Brock, Angelo
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Flower Foods, Inc., et al. v. Brock, Angelo. This means the Court will review the lower court's decision in this case.
events.why_relevant: Granting certiorari indicates the Supreme Court's interest in reviewing the legal issues presented.

events.title: Hamza v. Yandik, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion to direct the Clerk to file a petition for a writ of certiorari out of time in the case of Hamza v. Yandik, et al. This decision means the petitioner cannot proceed with their case in the Supreme Court due to a missed deadline.
events.why_relevant: This order underscores the importance of procedural deadlines in the judicial process.

events.title: Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Constr., Inc.
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Constr., Inc. This allows the Court to review the decisions made by lower courts in this case.
events.why_relevant: Granting certiorari allows the Supreme Court to address potentially significant legal issues.

events.title: Landor v. LA DOC, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of the Solicitor General for leave to participate in oral argument as amicus curiae and for divided argument in the case of Landor v. LA DOC, et al. This allows the Solicitor General to present additional perspectives during the oral arguments.
events.why_relevant: This order highlights the role of the Solicitor General in influencing court proceedings.

events.title: Little, Gov. of ID, et al. v. Hecox, Lindsay, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court deferred the respondent's request to dismiss the case as moot pending oral argument in the case of Little, Gov. of ID, et al. v. Hecox, Lindsay, et al. This decision delays the determination of mootness until after oral arguments are heard.
events.why_relevant: This order affects the timing and potential outcome of the case.

events.title: Rogalski v. PA Dept. of Education
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion for leave to file a petition for a writ of certiorari with the supplemental appendix under seal in the case of Rogalski v. PA Dept. of Education. This procedural action allows the petitioner to submit additional confidential materials for the Court's consideration.
events.why_relevant: This order affects the transparency and confidentiality of court proceedings.

events.title: United States v. Hemani, Ali D.
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of United States v. Hemani, Ali D. This decision means the Court will review the case, which involves the United States as a party.
events.why_relevant: This order signifies the Supreme Court's willingness to examine the legal questions involved in the case.

events.title: Certiorari Denied in Boyd v. Ivey
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Boyd v. Ivey, Governor of Alabama. The application was initially presented to Justice Thomas, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of Anthony Boyd's death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.

events.title: Supreme Court grants divided argument and time enlargement in pending cases
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted a motion for divided argument and enlargement of time for oral argument in the pending cases of Learning Resources, Inc., et al. v. Trump, President of U.S., et al. (No. 24-1287) and Trump, President of U.S., et al. v. V.O.S. Selections, Inc., et al. (No. 25-250). A total of 80 minutes is allotted for oral argument, with 40 minutes for the Solicitor General, 20 minutes for one advocate on behalf of the private parties, and 20 minutes for one advocate on behalf of the state parties. The motion by Susan Webber, et al. for leave to participate in oral argument as amici curiae, for divided argument, and for enlargement of time was denied.
events.why_relevant: The order affects the procedural conduct of oral arguments in significant cases involving the President and private parties.
